boy1: Is a straight neck on an X-ray the cause of neck pain? Studies comparing people with and without pain, pillows and neck collars, desk and sleep advice, and six exercises to ease the neck.
boy3: A straight neck means that, on a side-view X-ray, the neck vertebrae – which normally sit in a gentle forward curve (lordosis) – look straightened. It is a common diagnosis in Turkey and often causes worry. Yet research shows that straightening is seen about as often in people with neck pain as in people without it. Treating the pain focuses less on the curve on the X-ray and more on how the neck is used.

boy11: Is straightening the cause of the pain?
boy12: One study looked at the neck X-rays of 107 people over the age of 45; half of them had neck pain. A straight or backward-curved neck was seen about as often in those with pain as in those without. The authors concluded that these findings in a person with pain are most likely coincidental and do not explain the cause of the pain.
boy13: Another study, by chiropractic researchers, found neck pain more often in people whose curve was under 20 degrees. This study shows only an association at one point in time; it does not prove that straightening causes pain.
boy15: Straightening on an X-ray is not a disease in itself; it is also seen in many people with no pain.
boy16: Common causes of neck pain include sleeping with the neck in an awkward position and poor posture at a desk for long periods.
boy17: The aim of treatment is to reduce pain and help the neck move comfortably again, rather than to change the curve.
boy20: Unless your doctor says otherwise, it is better to keep moving your neck; a neck collar is not recommended.
boy21: You can sit upright, gently roll your shoulders back, and avoid keeping your neck in the same position for a long time.
boy22: You can use a low, firm pillow and keep your head in line with your body. Sleeping on your front strains the neck.
boy24: A cold pack or heat wrapped in a towel and short-term painkillers can bring relief.

boy28: Can a straight neck be corrected?
boy29: The real goal is not to change the curve but to reduce pain and help the neck move comfortably; regular exercise and keeping the neck moving during the day help with this.
boy30: Should I use a special pillow or a neck collar?
boy31: The UK’s National Health Service (NHS) suggests a low, firm pillow for neck pain; a neck collar is not recommended, because keeping the neck moving is better. You can choose by trying a pillow that feels comfortable to you.
boy32: Are dizziness and headaches caused by a straight neck?
boy33: Headaches can come from the neck, but dizziness has many other causes. Rather than putting these symptoms down only to the straightening on an X-ray, it is better to have them assessed by a doctor. You can also see our headache and dizziness guides.
boy34: Does bending over a phone cause a straight neck?
boy35: Staying bent forward in the same position for a long time can cause tension and pain in the neck. Bringing the screen closer to eye level, taking frequent breaks and moving the neck in different directions helps.
